description: Issue & Ruling Ledger initialized. Append-only log of all Shariah governance findings.

Arba'een (2-20) hadith 'Indeed Husayn is the lamp of guidance and the ark of salvation' cited as 'Reported in various sources'. No book, no number. Text authenticity is DISPUTED — not found in any of the six canonical collections. Violates JPP reflections.minimum_citation and hadith.misattribution (critical_violation).

Arba'een (Safar 20) is primarily a Shia observance marking 40 days after Karbala. Including it as a standard Islamic occasion violates JPP posture.sectarian_content: prohibited and posture.madhhab: neutral. Not universally observed across Sunni traditions.

JPP hadith.grading_display: mandatory — but NONE of the 365 daily reflections or 21 special day reflections display hadith authentication grading (Sahih/Hasan/Da'if). This is a systemic violation affecting ALL content. Each hadithSource field contains only book name + number, never grading.

Shab-e-Barat (8-15) uses Ad-Dukhan 44:1-3 ('Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night'). Majority of classical tafsir scholars (Ibn Kathir, Tabari, Qurtubi) identify this 'blessed night' as Laylat al-Qadr, NOT the 15th of Sha'ban. Applying it to Shab-e-Barat is a contextual misattribution of Quranic meaning.

Shab-e-Barat hadith (Ibn Majah 1390) about Allah looking at creation on mid-Sha'ban — grading is disputed. Some scholars grade it Hasan, others Da'if. JPP weak_hadith policy: 'labeled_clearly_if_shown'. No grading label is displayed. Full text also omits the hadith's exception clause.

Last Day of Tashreeq (12-13) cites hadith from 'Ahmad 7/224' (Musnad Ahmad). Musnad Ahmad is NOT in the JPP hadith.collections_allowed list (only six canonical collections approved). Content may be valid but source is outside governance scope.

Mawlid an-Nabi (3-12) inclusion as special day. While celebrated by majority of Muslims globally, it is considered bid'ah by a significant minority (Salafi, some Hanbali scholars). JPP posture.madhhab: neutral. The niyyah text itself is non-controversial (sending salawat), but the structural elevation as a 'special day' may breach neutrality.

The 365 daily reflections (src/data/dailyReflections.ts) and 21 special day reflections (src/data/specialDayReflections.ts) are not registered in CSR.json. JPP governance.change_tracking_for_religious_data: true requires all Islamic content to be tracked. No SHA-256 hash, no approval status recorded.
evidence: governance/CSR.json — no entries for dailyReflections or specialDayReflections datasets

description: Shab-e-Barat (8-15) niyyah mentions 'He descends to the lowest heaven'. The concept of Allah's descent (nuzul) is a point of theological difference between Athari (literal), Ash'ari (metaphorical), and Maturidi schools. Presenting it without qualification may breach madhhab neutrality for a sensitive aqidah topic.

Sahih al-Bukhari 1901 (Laylat al-Qadr standing in prayer hadith) is used in BOTH special day 9-25 AND 9-27. While not technically incorrect, it reduces content diversity for the most important nights.
